main.description: A claim by this account holder that they contributed to a specific work. THIS IS THE ONLY BRIDGE between the CV namespace and the bibliography namespace, and the central design decision of both: because bibliographic metadata (pub.paper.reference) is separated from the authorship claim, a reference has exactly one shape whether it is your paper or someone else's, nothing is stored twice, and the claim itself becomes an independently attestable object (see id.career.attestation). A claim here is self-asserted and unverified by construction; verification is an AppView concern, computed from Crossref/ORCID agreement and from third-party attestations.

reference.description: StrongRef to a pub.paper.reference record, normally one in this same repo.

totalAuthors.description: Stored so 'N of M' can be rendered without loading the full reference.

isLastAuthor.description: Separate from position because in the life sciences last authorship denotes seniority, not order.

equalContribution.description: Part of a co-first or co-equal group (the '*' footnote).

peerReviewStatus.description: Kept here rather than on the reference because review status is a property of this account's relationship to the work at a point in time, and because different CV formats sort by it. WARNING: 'underReview' reveals that a manuscript is out and often implies where; consider omitting the record entirely until acceptance rather than relying on `disclosure`.

venueType.description: 'proceedingsAbstract' is a 予稿集 abstract, 'bulletin' is a 紀要 (institutional journal), and 'commentary' is a 解説記事. All three are ubiquitous in Japanese CVs, are usually filed under MISC, and have no place in the international venue vocabularies.

scope.description: 国際/国内 distinction, required by many Japanese and tenure-track reporting formats.

acceptanceRate.description: Venue acceptance rate as printed, e.g. '18.4%'. Conventional in computer science CVs, meaningless elsewhere -- optional and never inferred.

authorNameUsed.description: The name form under which this work was published, when it differs from the current profile name (name changes, romanisation variants). Essential for disambiguation.

disclosure.description: ADVISORY ONLY, NOT PRIVACY. atproto records are public; 'unlisted' merely asks well-behaved clients to omit this from default CV renders. Anything that must stay secret must not be written to a PDS at all.

outputCategory.description: Which CV section this output belongs in. THIS IS AUTHOR-DECLARED AND NOT DERIVABLE from the reference's type or venue. researchmap splits outputs into 論文 / MISC / 書籍等出版物, and where a given item lands is a judgement the author makes: a Japanese-language 解説 in a society journal, a conference 予稿集 abstract, and a translated review all sit in MISC for one researcher and in 論文 for another. Any system that infers this will silently misfile hundreds of records -- this profile has 171 論文 against 336 MISC.

contributionType.description: Nature of the contribution to a book or edited volume, matching the researchmap 担当 vocabulary: 単著 / 共著 / 編者 / 分担執筆 / 翻訳 / 監修. Required for book records, meaningless for journal articles. 'supervision' is 監修, a credited role in Japanese publishing with no direct English equivalent.

isFeatured.description: Marked by the author as a principal work (researchmap 主要な業績). Lets a dossier render a 'selected publications' section without a second curated list going stale alongside the full one.
